title: AI and Oil Imports Push US Trade Deficit to $105.6B Record
summary:
Demand for foreign crude and artificial intelligence infrastructure drove the U.S. trade gap to its widest level since early 2025 in August. Refiners' need for heavy Canadian barrels while Brent crude stayed near $100 pushed industrial supply imports up 16.6%. Simultaneously, the race for AI capacity increased capital goods imports by 4%, causing the trade gap with Taiwan to hit $18.1 billion in July and surpass the $15.2 billion deficit with China.

The total trade deficit reached $105.6 billion, exceeding the $102.1 billion analyst estimate and July's revised $92.8 billion. According to Commerce Department data, imports grew 4.3% to $420.75 billion, while exports rose 1.4% to $315.18 billion. The imbalance has widened $34.4 billion over the last two months and marks a record high if volatility from Liberation Day swings is excluded.

U.S. TRADE DEFICIT SURGES TO $105.6 BILLION

The U.S. trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion in August vs. $102 billion expected, up sharply from July’s revised $92.8 billion.

Imports jumped 4.3% to $420.75 billion, outpacing a 1.4% rise in exports to $315.18 billion.

The goods deficit hit $136.57 billion, while the services surplus stood at $31 billion.

selectedTweets.text:
🇺🇸US trade deficit jumps to $ 105.6bn on OIL and AI

Imports rose 4.3%. 
Exports rose 1.4%.

2 things are driving it.

1️⃣The first is oil🛢️ 
The 🇺🇸US exports more petroleum than it imports, but its refiners still buy foreign crude, mostly heavy barrels from 🇨🇦Canada. 
With Brent near $100, each of those barrels costs more. Early data showed imports of industrial supplies up 16.6% in August, led by petroleum.

2️⃣The second is AI🤖
Most data centre hardware is built abroad. 
Imports of capital goods rose 4% in August, after imports of computers and accessories jumped $ 13.5bn in July alone.

You can see it in where the deficit sits. 
In July the gap with 🇹🇼Taiwan was $ 18.1bn, bigger than the gap with 🇨🇳China at $ 15.2bn. 🇲🇽Mexico ($ 27.5bn) and 🇻🇳Vietnam ($ 23.3bn) were bigger still.

Tariffs were meant to narrow the gap. 
Through July the deficit was 29.6% below the same period of 2025, although early 2025 was inflated by companies stockpiling ahead of tariffs.
But companies racing to build AI capacity have no domestic supply of servers at scale and refiners need crude whatever it costs.

The open question is oil... If Brent stays near $100, the import bill stays high into Q4.
